what: browserscan.net traced four ways with tools/fingerprint/stall-trace.mjs, to find what the hardware card waits on.
rootCause: FileReader dispatched its load event synchronously, from inside readAsDataURL. browserscan's canvas-vs-OffscreenCanvas check (dist/Dd65eSZK.js, function Q) registers that listener on the line AFTER the read, inside a promise only that listener resolves -- so the listener was attached to an event that had already fired, the promise never settled, and every card downstream of it stayed a placeholder. Nothing threw, which is why earlier error hooks found nothing.
whyTheGpuStringMattered: Q runs only when the renderer string is not a software renderer, so claiming a real GPU is what put the engine on that path for the first time. The Apple strings were innocent; see browserscan-apple-gpu-b1-renderer-sweep.json.
theSiteCode: function Q(){...const t=new OffscreenCanvas(240,60)...const c=n.toDataURL();return yield new Promise(_=>{t.convertToBlob().then(r=>{const d=new FileReader;d.readAsDataURL(r),d.addEventListener("load",function(i){_(i.target.result===c)},!1)})})}

measuredEventTiming.note: Both engines read the same blob and end with the same result; only the timing differs. Measured directly, not inferred from the trace.

pendingPromisesInSiteCode.note: The 5P8G9WMc.js:2:678 promises are pending in every run, including the ones that finish -- ip-api retry timers, not the stall. Chrome's six are all bare then() links with no site frame left in the stack.
